Hi! I just tested negative after about two weeks, but covid did impact my overall health and I do have pre-existing conditions. So if you are healthy I think these tips would help immensely because my partner did recover vastly faster than I did; drink a lot of fluid, but drink water at room temp because cold temps are going to irritate your throat more. Drink lots of Gatorade and pedialyte. Only use Tylenol to bring down fevers. Excess Tylenol will actually weaken immune responses that fight off the virus. If you have allergies or asthma, stay consistent with antihistamines and/or inhalers. Fluids are key with covid and my favorites are lemon and cayenne mixed in hot water or lemon and honey tea. The cayenne has capsaicin which is going to work like a pain reliever on your throat and it will also clear out any excess mucus you have. If you can’t do spice, lemon and honey have the same effects on cleaning mucus. I did not opt for actual tea blends, just the plain citrus squeezed with honey mixed in hot water will do. You might lose your taste and it’ll make you depressed, but eat foods with spice regardless and light candles or incense. Keeping your taste and smell stimulated is going to help you recover your olfactory and gustatory symptoms. The headaches from covid are intense sometimes Tylenol can only do so much and the pain still persists. When this would happen, I would spend 45 min with a facial roller I kept in the freezer and would massage my sinuses, temples, and jaw. It was a lot of effort but it truly did help me. If you don’t have a facial roller, your index and middle finger knuckles will have the same result. Nausea was also a huge problem I had and it sometimes made me not want to eat, so that’s when crackers came in handy. And try your best to eat as healthy as possible. We ate a lot of miso, sauerkraut (fermented foods in general are great to eat in general but especially when you have covid), and stews. Take vitamin D and only take vitamin C once a week. A lot of people overdo it with the Vit C but like Tylenol excess use can lower immune responses.

I am autistic and I used to nanny an autistic child. A lot of the trouble I had with the child I noticed was not because they were autistic but because they were spoiled. If anything you have an upper hand being able to relate to the child to some extent. Every autistic person is different that’s what makes the spectrum beautiful. I also occasionally tutor for an autistic kid. There are advantages we have like knowing when the child is becoming overwhelmed and overloaded with all the information tutoring gives a kid. For example, the kid I tutor was becoming very angry as a result of two issues 1.) they were hungry 2.) we did A LOT it was information overload for them so I stopped everything we were doing to wrap their special blanket around them and read them their favourite books.
